transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2025-09-18 14:30 UTC
- Duration: 48 minutes
- Attendees: Alex Monroe (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Jonah Li (CSM), Maya Patel (Tesseract Head of AI), Evan Cruz (Eng Manager), Samira Noor (SRE), Luis Herrera (Procurement)

Auto-summary (auto):
- Quick operational health check: usage trends, cost anomalies, and short-term capacity.
- Discussed options for smoothing peaks (bursting, dedicated pools, prefix caching).
- Agreed to run a focused benchmark with SREs next week; Redwood to provide pricing delta for burst vs reserved.

Topics:
- Current usage and spike patterns
- Cost hotspots and token distribution
- Reliability incidents and mitigation (fallbacks, regional routing)
- Short-term roadmap and runbook sharing

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (AE): ok everyone, thanks for making time. quick agenda — usage, costs, reliability, then next steps. maya, want to kick off with how traffic looked last month?
[00:15] Maya (Head of AI): yeah thanks alex. so september was weird — we had two sharp spikes on the 3rd and 11th, both tied to batch scoring jobs, not web. peak RPS hit about 5.6k for short windows, typical baseline ~800. the billing also spiked, obviously.
[00:35] Evan (Eng Manager): to add, a lot of the tokens were from long-context sessions, users pasting long carts and conversation history. we maybe should cull session retention or use KV cache more aggressively.
[00:52] Priya (SE): got it. from the Redwood side we saw high KV cache miss rate on those days — means the prefix caching didn't save as much as expected. can you confirm those batch jobs used dynamic prompts?
[01:08] Maya: yes they did, and there was also an A/B test that concatenated logs into prompts. not ideal.
[01:20] Samira (SRE): side note, our alarms tripped because of 95th percentile latency crossing 420ms during spikes. that caused downstream timeouts in the recommendation service.
[01:36] Alex: thanks. so two levers: reduce tokens per request (prompt engineering) and change serving config: dedicated pool vs hosted with burst. priya — quick reminder on cost tradeoffs?
[01:50] Priya: sure. hosted with burst is simplest: you pay on-demand delta when peak occurs, but unit cost is higher. dedicated reserved capacity lowers per-token costs for sustained load but needs commit and we size GPUs. there's also hybrid: reserved baseline + burst to handle spikes. from your pattern, we can model a small dedicated pool for baseline and let burst cover the 10-15% spikes.
[02:20] Luis (Procurement): what's the SLA difference if we use reserved vs hosted? also curious about compliance controls — we need audit logs and SSO routing for app teams.
[02:35] Jonah (CSM): reserved comes with an SLA addendum; we can include higher uptime guarantees and retention options. for audit we have access logs and can integrate with your SIEM; will share the SOC2/ISO summary deck.
[02:50] Evan: one pain is our infra is in a hybrid cloud, some services on-prem. would Redwood Private be an option for parts of the workload? and how much extra ops surface for us?
[03:05] Priya: yes Private is an option — we provide a VPC-deployed control plane and an on-prem inference bundle. it does require joint ops: kube config, KMS integration, and network setup. we'll share runbook snippets; we can also offer a short pilot to validate.
[03:28] Maya: curious about quantization recommendations — we saw a small quality delta on some reranking outputs when we tried an int8 variant. any tips?
[03:40] Priya: int8 can be safe for embeddings and many generative flows, but for rerankers or e2e evaluation we usually run eval sets. Redwood Optimize will propose quant profiles per workload. we'll run a quick eval next week as part of the bench.
[04:00] Samira: on the reliability side we want to understand fallback behavior — if a model variant is unavailable can requests route to a smaller model automatically? and will that be seamless to callers?
[04:12] Alex: yes we have smart routing/fallbacks; they can be configured per route. but a smaller model may change token usage and latencies, so you need to handle degradations. we'll show traffic shaping and graceful degrade patterns in the runbook.
[04:35] Evan: can we get per-route token breakdowns? our finance team wants to see which endpoints are the cost drivers.
[04:45] Jonah: yes the Console gives per-route, per-token, and token-type breakdowns. we'll export a sample report for you.
[04:55] Maya: also worth noting: on the 11th we hit a config drift where two canary routes were misrouted to the wrong region, which pushed traffic to a higher-latency cluster. how do we protect against that?
[05:12] Priya: guardrails: route policies, region pinning, and monitoring alerts. we can add a pre-deploy lint in your CI to catch region mismatches. we'll share our playbook.
[05:30] Luis: on procurement timeline — if we want reserved capacity for Q4, when do we need to commit?
[05:38] Alex: typically a 30-day lead for capacity provisioning; commit terms can be monthly or annual. if you want to test pilot first, we can start with a small reserved pool in two weeks.
[05:50] Evan: performance bench — we want to simulate our peak-day traffic and confirm 95th percentile under 300ms for the recommender. can Redwood run that or do we need to provide traffic generator?
[06:05] Priya: we can run it jointly. please provide two sample peak-day traces; we'll replay and run with SE + your SRE. expected time ~60 minutes for the bench, then we produce a report.
[06:22] Maya: what's the expected cost delta for a small reserved pool vs pure hosted? ballpark numbers are fine.
[06:30] Alex: ballpark — for your baseline (~800 RPS steady) a small dedicated setup could reduce per-token cost by roughly 30-40% compared to pure on-demand. bursts still cost more but overall monthly spend often drops. i'll send a model with numbers.
[06:48] Evan: any security blockers? our legal raised questions on data residency and keys. we use GCP KMS and some customer keys; need to know if Redwood can integrate with our KMS and support BYOK.
[07:02] Jonah: yes BYOK supported for Private and Dedicated via KMS integrations. hosted has envelope encryption options and can integrate with your enterprise KMS through the VPC path. we'll attach the KMS integration doc.
[07:20] Samira: there's also the audit requirement: we need immutable logs for 1 year and SSO via SAML. is that standard?
[07:29] Alex: standard for enterprise plans — retention and SSO are configurable. will include in the doc package.
[07:40] Luis: on invoicing — will reserved pools be invoiced monthly with commitments? also need line-item visibility for chargebacks.
[07:49] Alex: yes monthly invoicing with commitment tiers; Console exports CSVs for finance and you can enable token-level tagging.
[08:00] Maya: ok recap please and next steps?
[08:05] Alex: recap: Redwood to send pricing sheet with burst vs reserved scenarios, Priya to share runbook + bench scripts, customer to send two peak-day traces, schedule bench next week. action items in the notes.
[08:20] Evan: sounds good. small ask: can we get a quick checklist for on-call runbook integration so SREs can onboard?
[08:28] Priya: yes we'll include a checklist and a proposed alert threshold template.
[08:34] Maya: thanks all.
[08:36] Alex: thanks everyone — we'll follow up via email and slack.
